title: n8n SOC 2: What It Covers and Which Plans (2026)

body_markdown:
## Activepieces controls against the same checklist


Five controls answer the written-answers list at Activepieces. They're SSO and SCIM, custom RBAC, audit logs, a managed cloud in an EU or US region, and self-host with air-gap. Its SOC 2 programme is in progress, and the penetration test summary, DPA and sub-processor list are available on request.


Which one applies depends on where your workflows run, and that decides what a report can vouch for.


### Managed cloud in an EU or US region


On the managed cloud, Activepieces runs the service and you pick an EU or US region. Its SOC 2 programme is in progress, and the penetration test summary, DPA and sub-processor list are available on request.


So ask for the penetration test summary, DPA and sub-processor list, and check their scope against the hosted service you'd actually use.


For residency, region choice matters: your workflow data stays in the region you selected, which is the answer a GDPR-minded reviewer is looking for. It doesn't make your own flows or third-party connections part of the audit.


### Self-host and air-gap


A self-hosted install runs on your infrastructure, so the vendor's report doesn't cover it. Treat that as the point rather than a gap: you can read the compose file and the source tree, and you decide what leaves the network.


With an air-gapped deployment, **workflow data never crosses your boundary** , so a regulated team can keep data in its own environment. We make no HIPAA, BAA or ISO claim here. For a self-hosted install, your own controls are the ones that get audited.


These are the controls a reviewer will test against a live account, not a PDF:


- SSO and SCIM, so sign-in goes through your identity provider and leavers are deprovisioned from there rather than by hand.
- Custom RBAC, so a contractor gets only the flows and connections their job needs.
- Audit logs, so you can show who changed or ran what when asked.


Confirm which tier carries each one.


Activepieces Cloud lists Plus at $20 a month and Team at $200 a month, with Ultimate quoted through[https://www.activepieces.com/sales](https://www.activepieces.com/sales) , and in the repository the enterprise directories (` packages/ee/` ) sit under a separate commercial licence from the MIT-licensed core, so anyone deploying in production cannot rely solely on the open-source code.
